cover.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: 16:9 scientific editorial cover for a critical review of neural-network interpretability.
Primary request: A sophisticated, restrained cut-paper and gouache collage showing how different image categories can share one visual contour. On a pale warm-gray flat paper ground, two large separated tactile paper fragments: the upper face of a cat at left, a simplified front of a car at right. The cat's brow/nose contour and the car's hood/headlight contour each form an unmistakable matching broad V. A small V-shaped cut-paper aperture hovers slightly in front of each contour, revealing the shared shape while leaving enough of each object to recognize. Flat frontal collage, not a realistic device. Two different objects, one visually similar contour; an observation inviting investigation, not a fully decoded network.
Style/medium: original editorial gouache and hand-cut paper, dry brush edges and subtle paper fibers, architectural clarity with handmade warmth. Graphite charcoal, dusty coral and muted sage on warm gray; strong grayscale separation and generous negative space. Wide 16:9 composition, all meaningful objects comfortably inside the central safe area, readable at thumbnail size.
Constraints: no text, numbers, letters, formulas, logos, graphs, arrows, neurons, robot heads, brains, circuits, glowing webs, magic, padlocks or triumphant solved-puzzle imagery. Do not reproduce an existing publication cover or identifiable artist style. This is an artistic metaphor, not real scientific data or an activation heatmap. Avoid perspective corridors and grids of windows. Output a landscape 16:9 illustration.
cover.postprocessing: Minor edge crop to exact 16:9; WebP encoding without EXIF/GPS/ICC metadata.
